title: Manjari 7. The Branches of Srinivasa Acharya
html:
Srinivasa's family — wives, sons and daughters; disciples: Ramachandra and Govinda Kaviraja, Vyasa Acharya, the Chattarajas, the Chakravartis, Kanchanagaria, Rupa Ghataka, Vira Hambira and others; guru, Krishna and Vaishnava are one

[p. 101]

Tudi-raga.

1Bow down to Sri Krishna Chaitanya with His associates —
the limit of compassion, besides whom there is no other.

2Begging them Himself, He distributes the highest goal to the fallen;
the name "Purifier of the fallen" has now come true.

3I shall tell one thing more — hear its secret;
if your heart is firm, you will surely find joy.

4Sri Acharya Thakura accepted a multitude of disciples;
so that they may be known, I write of the chief ones.

5Who came earlier and who later I do not know;
I list all the names in a single place.

6Even if there is offense on my part in this,
still forgive me, all you merciful Prabhus.

7The mercy by which you gave shelter to your own —
that mercy is my refuge, I say for certain.

8The feet of all of you are my only shelter;
I bow down endlessly, (asking) that my offense be removed.

[p. 102]

9Sri Ishvari-jiu is the name of the elder Thakurani;
by Thakura's mercy she is the abode of all virtues.

10With her (Srinivasa) relished the pastimes of Radha and Krishna;
for this virtue the Prabhu's love for her was great.

11The name of the younger Thakurani is Sri Gauranga-priya;
the Prabhu was always happy seeing her conduct.1

12Vrindavana-vallabha Thakura is the eldest son,
younger than him is the son Sri Radhakrishna Thakura.

13Sri Hemalata Thakurani is their sister,
Sri Krishnapriya Thakurani is their sister;

14Sri Kanchan Thakurani and the Thakurani named Yamuna;
the youngest son of all is named Sri Govinda-gati.2

15Sri Ramachandra Kaviraja is a mine of all virtues:
the Prabhu himself called him his right arm.

16His younger (brother) is named Govinda Kaviraja,
through whom the Prabhu creates incomparable padas.

17One branch of Thakura is Sri Vyasa Acharya;
for the meeting with him see the sixth manjari.

18His son is Shyamadasa Acharya Mahashaya;
the Merciful One has shown mercy to him.

19Sri Ramakrishna Chattaraja Mahashaya
and his brother, Sri Kumuda Chattaraja —

20two greatly beloved by the Prabhu;
the all-in-all of both is the Prabhu's lotus feet.

[p. 103]

21The families of these two — (devoted) to Mahaprabhu;
the Prabhu accepted them all wholly:

22Sri Radhavallabha, Sri Gopijanavallabha,
Sri Govinda Raya, Sri Gauranga-vallabha,

23Sri Chaitanya Dasa, Sri Vrindavana Dasa,
Sri Krishna Dasa and others — with faith in the Prabhu's feet.

24The clan of Chattaraja Thakura — all are Chattarajas;
around them there is always an assembly of Vaishnavas.

25Malati Thakurani, (wife) of Kumuda Thakura Mahashaya —
on all the Merciful One has shown mercy.

26Rajendra Bandyopadhyaya, the son-in-law of Chattaraja Thakura,
is a vessel of the Prabhu's mercy, a pure Vaishnava.

27Sri Shyamadasa Chakravarti Mahashaya
and his younger brother, Sri Ramacharana Chakravarti:

28in spiritual matters both brothers are the Prabhu's disciples,
and by worldly relation both are his brothers-in-law.

29The younger was always with him to read the books of bhakti,
ever rejoicing in the pastimes of Radha and Krishna.

30Only when going abroad does (the Prabhu) set the arrangement,
so that there is no conflict between spiritual and worldly affairs.3

31In Kanchanagaria — Sri Gokula Dasa
and his younger brother, Thakura Sri Dasa.

32Gokula's son is Krishnavallabha Chakravarti,
who has the highest love for the Prabhu's feet.

[p. 104]

33Sri Dasa has three sons: the eldest, Jayakrishna Acharya,
his younger brother, Sri Jagadisha Acharya,

34and younger still, Shyamavallabha Chakravarti;
all see in them the manifest embodiment of prema.

35Sri Nrisimhadasa Kaviraja Mahashaya;
Narayana Kaviraja is his younger brother.

36Harivallabha Sarakara, Mathuranatha Mahashaya,
Sri Gopala Dasa, residing in Kanchanagaria.

37Rupa Ghataka Mahashaya, a resident of Yajigrama,
gave (the Prabhu) half his house as a dwelling.

38Sri Radhavallabha Dasa and Ramana Dasa Mahashaya —
the two sons of Kamadeva Mandala.

39Sri Govinda Chakravarti Mahashaya —
the one whom the Prabhu calls "Bhavuka Chakravarti".4

40Sri Karnapura Kaviraja, great of mind;
Sri Gopala Dasa Thakura, most virtuous.

41Sri Krishna Purohita is the pujari of Gaura-Thakura;
Sudhakara Mandala and Narayana Mandala — both companions.

42Narayana Mandala's brother is Sri Gopala Mandala,
a vessel of the Prabhu's mercy, mighty in bhajana.

43Sri Narayana Chaudhuri Mahashaya —
his home is at Rampura in Goyas pargana;

44most sweet are the service and pastimes of his Govinda,
whose abhisheka Acharya Thakura performed.

[p. 105]

45Sri Vallavi Dasa Kaviraja Mahashaya;
Sri Vanamali Kaviraja, full of the rasa of prema.

46Sri Raghu Dasa Thakura, Sri Mohana Dasa,
a vessel of the Prabhu's mercy — Sri Rama Dasa.

47Sri Shyama Bhatta and Sri Atmarama;
Sri Narika(?) Mahashaya, unbounded in prema.

48Sri Gopiramana Kaviraja and his brother Durgadasa;
King Vira Hambira,5 Sri Radhakrishna Dasa.

49Sri Jayarama Dasa Thakura of Kansona;
Sri Gokuladasa Kaviraja, a flood of prema:

50his former home was in Karai,
now he lives at Panchakot, in Shergarh.

51Sri Vamshidasa Thakura is a vessel of the Prabhu's mercy;
his former home was Budhair Bahadurpur;

52his shelter is the service of Sri Gopiramana-jiu;
the limit of his good fortune — who could describe it?

53Now his home is at Aminabazar.
These are (disciples) famous in the world — who can reach their end?

54In Virabhumi there are three kings among vaidyas;
of them the foremost is Bhagavan Kaviraja,

55his younger (brother) is named Sri Rupa Kaviraja;
Bhagavan's son is Nimu Kaviraja, an abode of virtues.

56So I have written the names of those I know;
and on reflection — how many more he has!

[p. 106]

57All of them are vessels of Sri Acharya Thakura's mercy;
whoever thinks otherwise of this even by a sesame seed —

58for that offense there is no deliverance for him.
Listen attentively to the essence of siddhanta:

59guru, Krishna and Vaishnava — the three are one;
if there is enmity toward one, all three destroy (such a person).

60By the Prabhu's mercy all have unbounded prema;
what can I say? — all this is known to the world.

61All the lords of my lord are my highest treasure;
this great hope I keep in my heart as everything.

62All are purifiers of the fallen, all are friends of the wretched,
all are embodiments of mercy, all are friends of the helpless.

63Effortlessly you delivered sinners;
take some trouble — accept me too.

64Without discrimination, all together, grant a particle of mercy:
let the desire of many births be fulfilled.

65Those whose all-in-all is Sri Rupa with his family —
for their joy this pastime is proclaimed.

66Wishing to describe this connection, the gurus and the rest,
Manohara Dasa tells the Anuraga-valli.

Thus ends, in the Srimad Anuraga-valli, the seventh manjari, called "The Description of the Branches of Srimad Acharya Thakura".

Notes

  1. Ishvari and Gauranga-priya are Srinivasa's two wives, as in the Karnananda (1.116–117) and the Prema-vilasa.
  2. According to the Karnananda (1), Kanchana-latika is Srinivasa's daughter; Yamuna is not named in the Karnananda. Govinda-gati is the Gati-Govinda of the Karnananda and the Prema-vilasa.
  3. The sense of the couplet is unclear; translated by sense.
  4. "Bhavuka" — "deeply feeling".
  5. The king of Vishnupura (cf. 6.209). Radhakrishna Dasa is a separate disciple (cf. Karnananda 1.225).
